note: Canonical coverage of the 31 topics in the visualization proposal. Templates are the implementation; topics are what a learner is taught. One template may teach several topics, and a topic may be partial or absent despite a related figure existing. scripts/audit_visuals.py reads this file and fails when a listed template does not exist, when an absent topic names one, or when a template teaches no topic at all.

topics.label: matrix multiplication as a geometric action
determinants as area and volume scaling
topics.note: area is drawn as the image of the unit square and changes continuously with det A; positive keeps orientation, negative reverses it, zero collapses the square onto a line. Volume scaling is a 3D claim and stays out of scope.

topics.label: triangles, circles and polygons
topics.note: the learner builds the polygon by adding, removing and dragging vertices, then applies a rotation, reflection, translation or dilation and reads the matrix, the vertex images, the largest side change and the area scale. There is no circle tool, no free-form curve and no 3D.

topics.label: coordinate geometry
topics.note: geo.coord lets a learner drag two points, read the distance and midpoint working with the substituted numbers, and move a second line to see where two lines meet, including parallel and coincident pairs. It does not cover polar coordinates, circles, rotated conics or three-dimensional distance.

topics.label: 3D solids and spatial relationships
topics.note: One solid of revolution is drawn: r(x) = 1 + 0.35 sin(1.6x) about the x axis, with a movable disk cross-section, orbit by drag or slider, volume by disks and lateral area. Arbitrary surfaces, composed solids, 3D transformations and intersections are not shown.

topics.label: conic sections
topics.note: shows which conic the equation Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 = 1 describes, from the sign pattern of the squared terms and the discriminant, with the degenerate rank-one case drawn as the pair of parallel lines it is. A parabola needs a linear term this equation family does not have, so it cannot appear here, and circles, ellipses and hyperbolas are drawn axis-aligned or rotated by the cross term only.

topics.label: complex multiplication as rotation and scaling
contour visualisation
topics.note: five functions (1/z, z, z squared, conj z, e to the z) along four path families (circle, ellipse, wavy closed curve, line segment), with the running value I(t) drawn as a vector and trace in a second plane, direction reversible, and the crossing reported rather than a number when the path passes through the pole. Closed-path pole detection samples 4000 points, so it is approximate. Residue theory, winding numbers, images of the interior and arbitrary expressions are not shown.

topics.label: probability distributions
topics.note: normal, uniform and exponential densities on one axis at equal standard deviation, with the probability each gives the same interval; discrete families are not included

supplementary.reason: linear systems are not one of the proposal's 31 topics; the elimination figure is required by the linear-transformation brief and teaches a different activity, so it is recorded here rather than inflating the topic list
